newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end up, rally for fifth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end up, rally for fifth straight day.

text.p: Stocks at Bombay bourses shrugged off early worries about profit-taking on Monday as fresh speculative bidding in front-bench stocks helped the market finish higher for the fifth session in a row, dealers said.
"The market trend is a bit confusing. An expected reaction only came from intra-day levels. The mood continues to remain buoyant," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities.
"People are still looking for a further rally."
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange(BSE) 30-share index fell to an intra-day low of 3,388.80, but rebounded to close 34.78 points, or 1.02 percent, higher at a provisional 3,453.10.
Dealers said Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's statement on Monday that the government had no intention as of now to raise prices of petroleum products aided market sentiment.

"As of now, the United Front government has no intention to take such a step," United News of India (UNI) quoted the Indian premier as saying in the southern state of Karnataka. He was responding to newspaper speculation about an immediate hike.

Some analysts, however said the market was due for a much-awaited correction. "Basically, this is a rally that will not sustain...there is a lot of speculative buying," said Basant Agarwal,head of equities at local firm JM Share & Stock Brokers.
Agarwal said foreign funds were buying defensive stocks in the hotel, power, petroleum and pharmaceutical sectors.
"Prices are going up on expectation of sops offered by the government...We expect the market to see some technical resistance at these levels," he said.

Dealers said foreign players were bidders in Cadbury, Brooke Bond and ACC. Tobacco major ITC surged 17.25 rupees to 363.0 in hectic speculation with over 4.13 million shares traded. SBI rose 0.25 rupees to 253.75 rupees, Reliance 2.50 to 223.50, MTNL 7.0 to 256.0, TISCO 3.75 to 189.0 and ACC 58.0 to 1,360.0.
